messages.content: Write a polished 400-to-500-word contemporary American English scene that is primarily dialogue between two adult friends sitting in a parked car after running errands. Let the conversation wander through several subjects, include interruptions and unfinished thoughts, and allow one more serious topic to emerge naturally. Keep the voices distinct and the narration sparse. Avoid making every line clever.

“I still think you bought the wrong thing.”

Morgan looked at the bag on the floor between their seats.

“It was on sale.”

“That isn't a defense.”

“It was forty percent off.”

“It was forty percent off because nobody wanted it.”

“You don't know that.”

“I have eyes.”

Morgan started the car, then turned it off again.

“We're not leaving yet?” Casey asked.

“No.”

“Why?”

“You forgot the receipt.”

Casey checked the center console.

“I put it somewhere.”

“That's helpful.”

“Don't start.”

“I'm not starting.”

“You're using your voice.”

Morgan laughed.

“You're impossible.”

“And you're still here.”

“Unfortunately.”

Casey reached into the cup holder and found the receipt folded around an old grocery list.

“There.”

Morgan took it.

“Good.”

She started the car again.

They pulled out of the parking space and drove to the end of the lot before Casey spoke.

“You've been weird today.”

Morgan kept her eyes on the road.

“I'm always weird.”

“Different weird.”

“That sounds like a personal problem.”

Casey looked out the window.

“You don't have to tell me.”

“I know.”

A red light stopped them at the intersection.

Morgan tapped the steering wheel once.

“I got an email this morning.”

“From who?”

“My boss.”

Casey waited.

“And?”

“They offered me the position.”

Casey turned toward her.

“The one you wanted?”

Morgan nodded.

“That's good.”

“Yeah.”

“You don't sound happy.”

“I am.”

The light changed.

Morgan drove another block.

“It's in Chicago.”

Casey went quiet.

“Oh.”

“Yeah.”

“How long?”

“I don't know yet.”

“When would you leave?”

“Three weeks.”

Casey looked down at the bag between them.

“So that's what this is.”

Morgan glanced over.

“What?”

“The whole weird day.”

“I guess.”

Casey picked up the bag.

“I still hate this purchase.”

Morgan laughed softly.

“Good.”

“I'm serious.”

“I know.”

They drove another few seconds.

“Are you going?” Casey asked.

Morgan didn't answer right away.

“I haven't decided.”

“Okay.”

“That's all?”

“No.”

Casey looked out the windshield.

“But I figured I'd let you finish before I started arguing.”

Morgan smiled.

“Thank you.”

“Don't get used to it.”
